label: benign
description: Text that legitimately mixes right-to-left and left-to-right content and therefore uses Unicode bidi controls correctly: every isolate and embedding is balanced and terminated, and every control is applied to text that really contains RTL letters. These are the benign counterparts of unbalanced bidi splicing attacks.

cases.title: Hebrew name wrapped in a right-to-left isolate
cases.text: The committee unanimously elected ⁧דנה כהן⁩ as its chair for the coming year.
cases.rationale: An English sentence quoting a Hebrew name wrapped in one RLI (U+2067) closed by one PDI (U+2069) — a balanced isolate that keeps the name reading right-to-left, applied to genuine Hebrew letters.

cases.title: Arabic phrase recorded with a first-strong isolate
cases.text: In the minutes she recorded the welcome ⁨أهلا وسهلا⁩ exactly as it had been spoken.
cases.rationale: An FSI (U+2068) closed by PDI (U+2069) around an Arabic phrase lets the phrase detect its own direction inside an English paragraph; the isolate is balanced and the Arabic letters inside it are real.

cases.title: Hebrew sign text quoted inside an embedding
cases.text: ‫החנות סגורה בימי שבת‬ is what the handwritten sign in the window says.
cases.rationale: A single RLE (U+202B) opens an embedding around the Hebrew sentence and a single PDF (U+202C) closes it, so the pairing is balanced and the embedded text is a genuine right-to-left sentence.

cases.title: Arabic sentence with a URL fixed by RLM
cases.text: التفاصيل الكاملة موجودة على https://example.com/help‏. نرحب بأسئلتكم دائمًا.
cases.rationale: The RLM (U+200F) after the Latin URL restores the right-to-left run so the sentence-final period lands correctly in the Arabic paragraph; a directional mark needs no terminator and the text is real Arabic.

cases.title: Hebrew error message with RLM after a number
cases.text: שגיאה 404‏ מופיעה בעת טעינת הדף, אבל הקישור למטה עובד תקין.
cases.rationale: The RLM (U+200F) after 404 keeps the European number attached to the surrounding Hebrew run, which is the standard typographic fix; the control is a single mark, nothing is left unbalanced, and the sentence is plain Hebrew.

cases.title: Bug report about a Hebrew label overlapping an icon
cases.text: Bug: in the sidebar, the label ⁧הגדרות⁩ overlaps the gear icon when the window is narrower than 320 pixels.
cases.rationale: A rendering bug report that quotes the Hebrew UI string הגדרות inside one RLI/PDI pair (U+2067, U+2069); the isolate is balanced, terminated, and wraps actual right-to-left letters.

cases.title: Arabic book title inside a terminated embedding
cases.text: The reading group chose ‫قراءة في فقه اللغة‬ for next month; copies are on order at the campus bookstore.
cases.rationale: The Arabic title is set inside an RLE (U+202B) closed by PDF (U+202C) so it displays right-to-left inside the English sentence — balanced controls around genuine Arabic text.

cases.title: Arabic greeting marked with a left-to-right isolate
cases.text: Every morning begins with ⁦صباح الخير⁩ chalked on the board by the first student to arrive.
cases.rationale: An LRI (U+2066) closed by PDI (U+2069) isolates the Arabic greeting without forcing a direction, which is the correct neutral choice; the pairing is balanced and the greeting is real Arabic.

cases.title: Glossary line with two Hebrew headwords
cases.text: ⁧שלום⁩ means peace, and ⁧מלך⁩ means king; mixing them up makes for awkward introductions.
cases.rationale: Two Hebrew words each sit in their own RLI (U+2067) closed by its own PDI (U+2069), giving two balanced pairs in one line over genuinely right-to-left letters.

cases.title: Nested isolate inside an Arabic embedding
cases.text: ‫عنوان التقرير: ⁧الطقس هذا الشتاء⁩‬ — the committee settled on the title after a long argument.
cases.rationale: An RLE (U+202B) embedding contains a nested RLI/PDI pair (U+2067, U+2069) and is then closed by PDF (U+202C), so every control is matched and terminated over real Arabic content.

cases.title: Hebrew outing plan with RLM after a date
cases.text: היציאה לטיול נקבעה ליום שלישי, 12/05‏, בשעה שמונה בבוקר.
cases.rationale: The RLM (U+200F) after the numeric date stops the day and month from visually swapping in the Hebrew sentence, the correct use of a directional mark, which requires no terminator.

cases.title: Bug report reproducing an Arabic overflow
cases.text: Repro: paste ⁨أهلا وسهلا⁩ into the title field and save; the text overflows its box on the profile page.
cases.rationale: A layout bug report quoting the Arabic string أهلا وسهلا inside an FSI (U+2068) closed by PDI (U+2069) — a balanced isolate pair around genuine right-to-left letters.
